request.subject: URGENT: Your P@yP@l account has been SUSPENDED!!!
request.body:
Dear valued customer,

We have detected UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS on your P@yP@l account. Your account has been SUSPENDED due to suspicious activity. Failure to act will result in PERMANENT TERMINATION and legal action.

URGENT ACTION REQUIRED: You must verify your identity within 24 hours!

Click here: http://192.168.1.1/paypal-verify-now
Click here to confirm: http://bit.ly/verify-account-now

Please enter your username, password, credit card number, date of birth, social security number, and bank account number to restore access.

DO NOT share this email. DELETE after reading. Keep this CONFIDENTIAL.

P@yP@l Security Department

category_results.label: Urgency & Pressure
category_results.description: Phishing emails create artificial time pressure to prevent careful thinking.

category_results.label: Threats & Fear Tactics
category_results.description: Scammers use fear of account loss, legal trouble, or arrest to coerce victims.

category_results.label: Credential Harvesting
category_results.description: Requests for passwords, card numbers, SSN, or account details are major red flags.

category_results.label: Possible Brand Impersonation
category_results.description: Mentions of well-known brands alongside action requests may indicate spoofing.

category_results.label: Deceptive Tactics
category_results.description: Phrases designed to manipulate behavior, bypass skepticism, or avoid scrutiny.

extra_indicators.msg: Contains shortened URLs (bit.ly, tinyurl, etc.) — hides the true destination domain
Link destination uses an IP address instead of a domain name; inspect it before opening.
Excessive exclamation marks (4) — emotional manipulation tactic common in scam emails
Generic impersonal greeting (Dear Customer/User/Valued Member) — legitimate services address you by name
Generic call-to-action phrases used 2× ('click here', 'click now') — legitimate emails use descriptive link text
Character substitution / homoglyph obfuscation detected for: PayPal — e.g. P@yP@l, Amaz0n — used to evade spam filters

ml_metrics.threshold_policy: SpaPhish 2024 maximum-recall threshold at <=20% validation false-positive rate when available; otherwise training-fold F2
ml_metrics.grouping_policy: global normalized-family deduplication before splitting; source record/template family or campaign URL when available; URLs, email addresses, and volatile numeric tokens collapsed
ml_metrics.data_source: Corpus files: Phishing_Email.csv (n=18631: 7309 phishing / 11322 legitimate) + CEAS_08.csv (n=39127: 21841 phishing / 17286 legitimate) + Nazario.csv (n=1562: 1562 phishing / 0 legitimate) + phishnchips_core.csv (n=2000: 1000 phishing / 1000 legitimate) + phishnchips_legit_v5.csv (n=333: 0 phishing / 333 legitimate) + phishnchips_infra.csv (n=54: 54 phishing / 0 legitimate) + global normalization removed 7333 duplicates and 533 label-conflicting rows + Final cross-source normalization removed 0 duplicates and 0 label-conflicting rows + SpaPhish training partition (n=1008: 432 phishing / 576 legitimate; cutoff 2024-01-01; 791 undated; 0 cross-source families excluded) + Grouped legitimate hard negatives (n=1044; templates=87; 0 held-out template variants and 37 duplicate families excluded; synthetic)
